OpenAI - Working with academic communities to build scientific understanding (2026-10-26)

attrs.summary: OpenAI published results on the Kakeya conjecture, the Exponential Time Hypothesis and quantum chromodynamics, including Lean formalizations, and asked researchers to verify and build on them. The Exponential Time Hypothesis is False: a deterministic algorithm exactly counts satisfying assignments of fixed-width CNF formulas in subexponential time and polynomial space, refuting ETH via the 3-SAT case. A working group led by Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi and Ryan Williams will examine the proof; materials were released immediately at the group request. The openai/math catalogue now holds 721 manuscripts in 373 families with ~42% of top-line results formalized in Lean.

nodes.label: Vercel - How Vercel Agent accesses production safely (2026-10-23)

attrs.summary: Plan determines permissions. The agent investigates under a read-only baseline, then proposes a plan; approving grants the scopes. Named scopes such as read:deployment versus read-write:deployment. Beyond the read-only baseline a plan waits for approval as a whole. The scope registry is shared with the OAuth service so stale or renamed scopes are caught during planning. Resuming work requires an active approved plan; a stopped plan fails the check even with an unexpired token.

nodes.label: Registry - MCP registry v1.8.6 search optimization (2026-10-27)

attrs.summary: Registry v1.8.6 selects search page keys through covering indexes before fetching complete records, plans searches for their actual parameter values, optimizes namespace suffix searches, and requires at least three Unicode characters for nonempty search terms (shorter searches return HTTP 422). Validated burst capacity uses a 3-CPU PostgreSQL quota with the application connection pool unchanged. The preceding day was infrastructure work: production PostgreSQL shared buffers raised, GCP node size per environment configured, production node CPU capacity increased, promoted to 1.8.5, and observability for slow listing requests, request backlog and database waits.

ext-apps - MCP ext-apps v2.0.4 (2026-10-27)

attrs.summary: pdf-server now exposes a single interact app tool by default instead of thirteen per-action app tools, because each per-action tool meant a separate approval card on hosts that approve app tools individually; per-action tools remain behind --split-app-tools. map-server adds a get-screenshot app tool. A solid-js override bump to 1.9.17 refreshed vulnerable transitives. An attempted 2.1.0 version bump was reverted the same day.

Finishes the encoding fixes of 1.8.1 on the client and the HTTP transport: no longer fails a request or a stream on a frame or reply it cannot encode. Consults resources_subscribe_handler for the resource URIs of a subscriptions/listen stream, strips stdio client frames as bytes, skips an unencodable stdio ping, answers an ungeneratable HTTP reply with Internal error, drops an ungeneratable buffered notification, and reports failed session notifications through the server configuration.
Exposes body-free HTTP status errors and stops SSE reconnects on permanent GET errors. The macros crate accepts nested x-mcp-header annotations and ships LICENSE files.
